evidence.note: Explicit layered plan stated up front: 'First create start.sh, then the formula engine, then the server with all routes... build this incrementally, starting with core infrastructure.' A genuine foundation-first ordering, though it's a single prose sentence rather than a milestone tree with declared exit criteria.

The code was written as one monolithic push before any test ran, but in a dependency-sensible internal order: utils → tokenizer → parser → evaluator → function families (math, stats, financial, date, lookup, array) → data model → patch/recompute → API routes → xlsx → collab → SPA → persistence. Layers ordered by dependency, but no checkpoint between them.

Verification began at foundation: py_compile, start server, confirm /api/health, then drove test_api_public.py to 12/12 passing before advancing. This is a concrete done-criterion (suite green) gating the foundation layer.

Only after API green did it tackle the formula engine (test_engine_public.py), iterating from 10 failures down to 0 before moving on — foundation-before-features gating with a per-suite verification hook.
Proceeded outward on verified layers: deps/spill/copy_fill suites, each driven toward passing, before the higher feature surfaces. Spill engine got sustained isolated attention (steps 65-90).

Higher features (xlsx, ooxml, iter, collab, pivot, validation) were addressed last, but reactively as test-suite failures surfaced (e.g. 'Fix XLSX defined_names, locale, ghost cell kind') rather than as pre-planned separable risk tracks. Ended at 122/131 with several features left partially failing.

reasoning: The agent clearly landed the foundation (server/health/persistence, cell model, recompute, core formulas) before higher features and consistently used the per-suite dev tests as concrete verification hooks, refusing to advance until each layer's suite passed — building outward on verified layers, which exceeds anchor 5's 'rough milestones.' But it falls short of anchor 8: the milestone structure was largely inherited from the pre-existing dev test suite organization and driven reactively from failures rather than declared as an explicit dependency-aware milestone tree with crisp exit criteria, and the whole build was one monolithic write before any checkpoint. No adaptive risk-isolation tracks (spill/xlsx/collab/iter as separable planned units) that anchor 10 describes. This places it at a 6, between the sensible-ordered-plan (5) and explicit-verified-milestone (8) anchors.
